new.title: Climb Marmaris Castle and its small museum
new.desc: The castle above the harbour was rebuilt by Süleyman the Magnificent in 1522 as a gathering point for his Rhodes campaign. Inside, the Marmaris Museum has amphorae, tombstones and lamps from Knidos, Datça and nearby sites.
new.tip: Go in the morning before the heat; views over the marina are best late afternoon. Check the current museum hours at the ticket desk.
new.q: Marmaris Kalesi ve Müzesi, Kemeraltı Mahallesi, Marmaris, Muğla

new.title: Wander the lanes of Marmaris old town below the castle
new.desc: The whitewashed lanes of Hisaraltı Street climb toward the castle, lined with Ottoman-era stone houses turned into cafés and craft shops. It is the quiet counterpart to the harbour front.
new.tip: Come in the evening when the lanes cool and the lamps come on; bring comfortable shoes for the cobbles.
new.q: Hisaraltı Caddesi, Kemeraltı Mahallesi, Marmaris, Muğla

new.title: Stand in the ancient port city of Knidos at Datça's tip
new.desc: Knidos was a Dorian city of Caria at the western tip of the Datça peninsula, famous for Praxiteles' Aphrodite statue in a circular temple. Remains include the round temple, theatre, two harbours and mosaics.
new.tip: The drive from Datça takes about 45 minutes; go early or late and bring water, as there is little shade.
new.q: Knidos Antik Kenti, Yazıköy Mahallesi, Datça, Muğla

new.title: See Kaunos and its cliff-cut rock tombs from the river
new.desc: Kaunos was a Carian harbour city whose temple-fronted rock tombs, mostly 4th century BC, face Dalyan across the river. The ancient city itself has a theatre, Roman baths and a harbour that silted up.
new.tip: Boats from Dalyan stop at the site; the tombs are best photographed from the water in the morning light.
new.q: Kaunos Antik Kenti, Dalyan Mahallesi, Ortaca, Muğla

new.title: Walk the ghost village among Stratonikeia's ruins
new.desc: Stratonikeia in Eskihisar is a Hellenistic and Roman city where villagers lived among the ruins until the 2000s. A colonnaded street, a theatre, gymnasium and bouleuterion stand beside abandoned Ottoman houses and a mosque.
new.tip: Allow two hours and wear sun protection; the site is large and open, with a museum at the entrance.
new.q: Stratonikeia Antik Kenti, Eskihisar Mahallesi, Yatağan, Muğla

new.title: Visit the Hecate sanctuary at Lagina
new.desc: Lagina was the sacred site of the goddess Hecate, linked to Stratonikeia by a Sacred Way along which the kleidos pompe procession ran. Excavations since 2016 have been uncovering its monumental temple and propylon.
new.tip: Combine with Stratonikeia in one half day; ask about site access, as excavation seasons affect visits.
new.q: Lagina Hekate Tapınağı, Turgut Mahallesi, Yatağan, Muğla

new.title: Cruise to Sedir Island (Cleopatra Beach) and ancient Kedrai
new.desc: The island in the Gulf of Gökova was the Carian city of Kedrai and is a protected archaeological site with a theatre, plus a beach of golden sand. Legend says Mark Antony shipped the sand from Egypt for Cleopatra.
new.tip: Day boats leave from Marmaris, Akyaka and Gökova; swim in summer and remember removing sand is illegal.
new.q: Sedir Adası İskelesi, Akyaka Mahallesi, Ula, Muğla

new.title: Stroll Muğla's Konakaltı old quarter and its chimneys
new.desc: Around 400 registered 18th and 19th century houses survive in Muğla's old quarter, with whitewashed walls and distinctive chimneys. Lanes such as Konakaltı and Saburhane Street are lined with restored mansions and craft shops.
new.tip: Visit in the morning; the pedestrian lanes are quiet outside weekends.
new.q: Konakaltı, Saburhane Caddesi, Muğla Merkez, Muğla

new.title: See the lead-domed Kurşunlu Mosque in Muğla
new.desc: Built around 1494 under Ottoman rule, the mosque takes its name from its lead-covered dome. It is one of the oldest Ottoman monuments of Muğla's old town.
new.tip: Remove shoes and dress modestly; outside prayer times visitors are usually welcome.
new.q: Kurşunlu Camii, Saburhane Caddesi, Muğla Merkez, Muğla

new.title: Step inside the Ulu Mosque of Muğla
new.desc: The Great Mosque of Muğla was built in 1344 under the Menteşe beys, making it one of the oldest buildings in town. It sits at the heart of the old quarter.
new.tip: Combine with the Konakaltı lanes; avoid prayer times.
new.q: Ulu Camii, Muğla Merkez, Muğla

new.title: Tour the old prison turned Muğla Museum
new.desc: The Muğla Museum occupies a 19th century building that served as a prison in Ottoman times. Its collections come from Stratonikeia, Kaunos, Knidos and other sites of the province.
new.tip: Allow an hour; it is indoors, so good for a hot afternoon.
new.q: Muğla Müzesi, Muğla Merkez, Muğla

new.title: Admire the Akyaka-style houses by Nail Çakırhan
new.desc: Poet and self-taught architect Nail Çakırhan, born in Ula in 1910, designed his own house in Akyaka and won the Aga Khan Award in 1983. The red-tiled, carved-wood houses of Akyaka follow the traditional Ula style he revived.
new.tip: Wander the streets behind the Azmak river; the Çakırhan house is a private home, so view from outside.
new.q: Nail Çakırhan Evi, Akyaka Mahallesi, Ula, Muğla

new.title: Hike up to the walls of ancient Loryma
new.desc: Loryma is a Carian fortified harbour on Bozukkale at the south-west end of the Bozburun peninsula, founded around the 7th century BC. Its walls and fortress sit above a sheltered bay.
new.tip: Reach it by boat from Bozburun or Selimiye, or by a rough track; take water.
new.q: Loryma Antik Kenti, Bozukkale, Bozburun Mahallesi, Marmaris, Muğla

new.title: Climb to the hilltop ruins of Amos above Turunç
new.desc: Amos was a Hellenistic city from around the 3rd century BC, with a theatre, temples and walls on a hill above the bay. It is a protected archaeological site with long sea views.
new.tip: Visit in the cooler morning; the walk up is steep.
new.q: Amos Antik Kenti, Turunç Mahallesi, Marmaris, Muğla

new.title: Wander old Datça's stone houses and bright doors
new.desc: Eski Datça is the old village north of the modern town, with stone houses, narrow streets and brightly painted doors. Many houses now hold small cafés, shops and meyhanes.
new.tip: Park outside the centre in summer, as parking is tight; evenings are most atmospheric.
new.q: Eski Datça, Datça, Muğla

new.title: Stroll the harbour village of Selimiye
new.desc: Selimiye is a quiet Bozburun-peninsula village known for its harbour, boatbuilding heritage and nearby ruins. Boats can moor alongside the waterfront cafes.
new.tip: Evenings suit the harbour; combine with Bozburun by road.
new.q: Selimiye Limanı, Selimiye Mahallesi, Marmaris, Muğla

new.title: Swim at İztuzu turtle beach
new.desc: İztuzu is a roughly 4.5 km sandbar beach near Dalyan, protected since 1988 and a major loggerhead nesting site. Nests are caged and access is limited at night during nesting.
new.tip: Go in the morning; follow rules on umbrellas and the evening closure.
new.q: İztuzu Plajı, Dalyan, Ortaca, Muğla

new.title: Take a boat down the Dalyan river reed channels
new.desc: Wooden boats glide from Dalyan through the reed-lined delta to Kaunos, the mud baths and İztuzu. Blue crabs, turtles and cliffside tombs appear on the way.
new.tip: Book at the quay in Dalyan; trips are common April to October.
new.q: Dalyan İskelesi, Dalyan, Ortaca, Muğla

new.title: Soak in Sultaniye's mud baths and thermal pools
new.desc: On the shore of Lake Köyceğiz, Sultaniye has sulphur springs at 39 to 42 degrees C and mud baths. It is often combined with a Dalyan boat trip.
new.tip: Expect a strong sulphur smell; wear old swimwear.
new.q: Sultaniye Kaplıcaları, Toparlar Mahallesi, Köyceğiz, Muğla

new.title: Swim and hike at Kumlubük bay
new.desc: Kumlubük is considered the most beautiful beach on the Bozburun peninsula, reached by road via Turunç and Bayır. Trekking trails start behind the bay.
new.tip: Plan a full day; bring cash for the beach club.
new.q: Kumlubük Plajı, Turunç, Marmaris, Muğla

new.title: Wade along the Kızkumu sandbar at Orhaniye
new.desc: Kızkumu stretches roughly 600 metres into Hisarönü bay as a shallow sandbar. The legend ties its name to the daughter of the king of Bybassos.
new.tip: Dolmuş minibuses run from Marmaris; go midweek in summer.
new.q: Kızkumu Plajı, Orhaniye, Marmaris, Muğla

new.title: Spend a beach day in Turunç
new.desc: Turunç is a pine-backed bay with a beach, small restaurants and boat connections to Marmaris and Amos. Reached by road via Bayır.
new.tip: Water taxis run in summer; arrive before noon.
new.q: Turunç Plajı, Turunç, Marmaris, Muğla

new.title: Swim in the long bay of Palamutbükü
new.desc: Palamutbükü on the Datça peninsula is known for a long pebbly beach and calm water, and is somewhat more upmarket than Ovabükü.
new.tip: Visit early in the summer to avoid crowds.
new.q: Palamutbükü Plajı, Datça, Muğla

new.title: Swim at Ovabükü in Mesudiye
new.desc: Ovabükü is the main beach of Mesudiye on the south shore of the Datça peninsula, with a long cove and cafés.
new.tip: Combine with the Archaeological and Folklore Museum nearby.
new.q: Ovabükü Plajı, Mesudiye Mahallesi, Datça, Muğla

new.title: Float or kayak the cold Azmak river at Akyaka
new.desc: The Azmak is a short, spring-fed river flowing into the Gulf of Gökova at Akyaka, lined with reeds and riverside restaurants. Locals paddle and swim in the cold water.
new.tip: Rent kayaks along the bank; summer midday is hot.
new.q: Azmak Nehri, Akyaka, Ula, Muğla

new.title: Try kitesurfing on Akyaka's windy bay
new.desc: Akyaka is known for afternoon winds in the Gulf of Gökova, which suits kitesurfing and windsurfing.
new.tip: Schools rent kit; best May to September.
new.q: Akyaka Plajı, Akyaka, Ula, Muğla

new.title: Walk the almond blossoms of the Datça peninsula
new.desc: Datça's hillside terraces have almond groves that bloom white and pink in late winter. Almonds and honey are the peninsula's agricultural signatures.
new.tip: Drive the road between Datça and Reşadiye in late February.
new.q: Datça Bademlik Bölgesi, Reşadiye, Datça, Muğla

new.title: Walk the Marmaris marina and waterfront at sunset
new.desc: Marmaris Yacht Marina is one of the biggest on the Turkish coast, with a waterfront promenade beneath the castle hill.
new.tip: Go at golden hour and finish with fish nearby.
new.q: Marmaris Yacht Marina, Marmaris, Muğla

new.title: Browse the Marmaris bazaar for spices, olive soap and honey
new.desc: The old bazaar next to the harbour sells spices, olive-oil soap, honey and textiles.
new.tip: Bargain politely; weekdays are calmer.
new.q: Marmaris Çarşısı, Kemeraltı Mahallesi, Marmaris, Muğla

new.title: Stroll the Köyceğiz lakeside promenade
new.desc: Köyceğiz is a lakeside town where tree-lined promenades face Lake Köyceğiz, with boat trips to Sultaniye and Dalyan.
new.tip: Sunset suits the promenade; mosquitoes are worst at dusk, so use repellent.
new.q: Köyceğiz Göl Kenarı Parkı, Cumhuriyet Mahallesi, Köyceğiz, Muğla

new.title: Watch the sunset at Hisarönü beach
new.desc: Hisarönü beach is ringed by palms and pines and is one of the sunset spots of the Marmaris area.
new.tip: Arrive an hour before sunset.
new.q: Hisarönü Plajı, Hisarönü, Marmaris, Muğla

new.title: Eat fresh fish at Olta beside the Azmak
new.desc: Olta sits among the reeds on the Azmak in Akyaka, serving fish, seafood and mezes.
new.tip: Ask for the fish of the day.
new.q: Olta Balık Restaurant, İnişdibi Caddesi No:46, Akyaka Mahallesi, Ula, Muğla

new.title: Order meze and fish at Kordon on the Azmak
new.desc: Kordon is a riverside restaurant on Yaşar Aytaç Sokak in Akyaka, serving meze and fish.
new.tip: Try the cold meze with rakı.
new.q: Kordon Restaurant, Yaşar Aytaç Sokak 26, Akyaka, Ula, Muğla

new.title: Eat river fish at Kordon in Dalyan
new.desc: Kordon Restaurant has been on the Dalyan riverfront since 1987, known for fresh fish.
new.tip: Book a riverside table for sunset.
new.q: Kordon Restoran, Dalyan Merkez, Ortaca, Muğla

new.title: Dine among turtles at Yalıçapkını
new.desc: Yalıçapkını is on the river near Dalyan where diners can spot turtles from the tables.
new.tip: Ask for a table close to the water.
new.q: Yalıçapkını Restoran, Dalyan, Ortaca, Muğla

new.title: Taste bademli ezme at Kekik in Datça
new.desc: Kekik Restaurant on Atatürk Caddesi in Datça serves Aegean meze including an almond-flavoured Cretan-style spread.
new.tip: Order several meze to share.
new.q: Kekik Restaurant, Atatürk Caddesi No:72, İskele Mahallesi, Datça, Muğla

new.title: Have breakfast facing the Kaunos tombs at Saklı Bahçe
new.desc: Saklı Bahçe Kahvaltı ve Çay Bahçesi is a riverside garden in Dalyan with views of the rock tombs.
new.tip: Go mid-morning for a long Turkish breakfast.
new.q: Saklı Bahçe Kahvaltı ve Çay Bahçesi, Dalyan, Ortaca, Muğla

new.title: Eat meze and fish at Balıkçım in Dalyan
new.desc: Balıkçım the Fisherman is a relaxed restaurant on a side street, popular with locals.
new.tip: Choose a fish from the display.
new.q: Balıkçım, Kbid Çarşısı 1, Dalyan Mahallesi, Ortaca, Muğla

new.title: Eat Muğla köfte at Zafer'in Yeri
new.desc: A grill house making only Muğla köfte, served over fried bread with onion salad.
new.tip: Go at lunch; köfte can run out by evening.
new.q: Meşhur Muğla Köftecisi Zafer'in Yeri, Muğla Merkez, Menteşe, Muğla

new.title: Try Muğla kebab at Çavuşun Yeri
new.desc: Çavuşun Yeri is a named place for Muğla kebab and köfte, per local food guides.
new.tip: Try the kebab with Muğla köfte.
new.q: Çavuşun Yeri Meşhur Muğla Kebabı ve Köftesi, Muğla Merkez, Menteşe, Muğla

new.title: Order calamari and shrimp at Deniz Balık in Marmaris
new.desc: Deniz Balık Yöresel Lezzetler is a family-run restaurant praised for calamari and fried shrimp.
new.tip: Order the calamari.
new.q: Deniz Balık Yöresel Lezzetler, Marmaris, Muğla

new.title: Book a table at Turgut Reis Balık in Marmaris
new.desc: A fish restaurant locals call among the best in Marmaris for fresh fish at reasonable prices.
new.tip: Reserve ahead.
new.q: Turgut Reis Balık Restaurant, Marmaris, Muğla

new.title: Sit at Eski Meyhane in old Datça
new.desc: Eski Meyhane at Osman Karaca Sokak in Eski Datça serves dishes with local fresh produce.
new.tip: Go in the evening.
new.q: Eski Meyhane, Osman Karaca Sokak 1, Eski Datça, Datça, Muğla

new.title: Dine at Culinarium on Datça harbour
new.desc: Culinarium is a seaside restaurant by the harbour, founded by a German woman who settled in Datça.
new.tip: Book a sunset table.
new.q: Culinarium, 64. Sokak No:20, İskele Mahallesi, Datça, Muğla

new.title: Taste almond-honey ice cream at Tekin Usta in Datça
new.desc: Tekin Usta Dondurma is known for ice cream with honey and almond.
new.tip: Visit after dinner.
new.q: Tekin Usta Dondurma, Kumluk Yolu No:50/A, İskele Mahallesi, Datça, Muğla
